Necessity uses the regular outer halfplane description, sufficiency uses n>=m to make that point the unique inner support maximizer. Reducing m inner phases modulo the n-gon facet-normal period yields k=m/gcd(n,m) equally spaced phases each repeated g times; arc occupancy is floor(kq) or ceil(kq) with exact fractional probabilities, proving full law and variance. Solving zero variance yields all deterministic radii. Taylor expansion and weak continuity yield the arithmetic critical-window limit, including integer transitions. equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Polarity of conv(P_n,rho P_m) is P_n^circ intersect (rho P_m)^circ. For an outer circumradius-one n-gon and inner circumradius rho m-gon, the polar circumradii equal sec(pi/n) and sec(pi/m)/rho; they are equal only if rho=cos(pi/n)/cos(pi/m)>=1 when n>=m, outside the strict rho<1 scope (except boundary). The equal-circumradius intersection classification therefore does not imply the new unequal-radius convex-hull distribution.
